sentence: Unbinned OmniFold adds an observable by adding an input to the step-1 and step-2 classifiers, without an explicit migration matrix or per-bin response tensor.

It avoids the combinatorial binning penalty of matrix unfolding but still has a dimensional cost: classifier training, acceptance and support coverage, sample sparsity and uncertainty quantification become more demanding as observables are added.
The primary methodological motivation is the absence of a practical analog of D'Agostini iterative Bayesian unfolding (IBU).

Three conditions under which it would not be added were fixed before any of the measurements that decide them was computed: one existing component, within two standard deviations of its own size, explaining at least half of both period-group patterns; a replica spread of the block's median per-cell width above half that width; or, in the median replica, less than half of the replica-built block's variance lying in the observed block's plane.
The conditions were set after the block's reported numbers had been read, and the second and third were not expected to fire.

That result establishes neither the block's size nor the absence of overlap: descriptively, one detector-response pair, a pion-interaction band with the meson response shift, reproduces one period's offset pattern within noise and part of the other two.

A first coverage test at these two tunes, specified before any pseudo-experiment was generated, for the covariance without the run-period block, with pseudo-experiments that also draw the flux, interaction and detector uncertainties (the lateral and normalization ones as surrogates, and $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{resp}}$ not at all), was stopped before any coverage pseudo-experiment ran.

At one of its gates, the ratio of each cell's uncertainty reproduced through the pseudo-experiments to that of the drawn covariance lay outside \fvval{cov1b-win-lo}--\fvval{cov1b-win-hi} in \fvval{cov1b-ncells-out} of the 16 cells, ranging from \fvval{cov1b-rho-min} to \fvval{cov1b-rho-max}.
Replacing the pseudo-experiments' values by the covariance's for any \fvval{cov1b-kmax-word} or fewer of the \fvval{cov1b-nbands} drawn bands does not bring every cell inside that window.
A staged redesign of that first test, at the two tunes and with the covariance rebuilt by the same procedure at each tune, also ended without a coverage result.

Each of its pseudo-experiments is drawn from a simulated world built from randomly drawn systematic universes; in each cell, that world's denominator is the first drawn universe's denominator plus each later universe's departure from the central-value denominator.
A rule fixed before the first stage ran stops that stage if any draw gives a non-positive denominator in a cell that is positive at the central value.
\lrval{stop-flagged} of the \lrval{stop-draws} draws did so, with at most \lrval{stop-maxcells} such cells in a draw, and the first stage stopped.
The record does not establish why those cells are non-positive.
At both tunes, an event-matching entry check stopped the earlier run because it compared \fvval{ll5d-a1a2-keys} weight keys and reported every row unmatched.
The repair, chosen after this stop, keyed both sides at \fvval{ll5d-a1a2-at} before any coverage pseudo-experiment was unfolded or graded, but after other gate readings were visible.
It changed no rule, threshold, bound or reporting cell.
Under the rule fixed before the result, the rerun is reported as descriptive: the criteria fixed in advance were applied, but a repair was chosen after an entry-check stop.
